TDG.thesis_one_line: Sole-source aircraft-parts monopoly with real pricing power, but growth is now heavily debt-and-acquisition-fueled and the price already assumes that keeps working for a decade.
TDG.horizon: not held at current price; revisit if net leverage falls toward 5x EBITDA or organic growth proves durable above 7% on its own
kill_criteria: Net debt/EBITDA As Defined (consolidated, per the company's own quarterly reconciliation table) exceeds 6.5x
GAAP net income growth is negative YoY for two consecutive fiscal quarters (already occurred once, FQ1 FY2026; a repeat would confirm a trend rather than a one-off financing-timing effect)
Organic sales growth (company's own disclosed figure, ex-acquisitions) falls below 7% for two consecutive fiscal quarters (vs. 7.4%/11.0%/13% in the last three quarters)
FY guidance is cut (not raised or maintained) at any subsequent quarterly release, versus the current $10,470-10,550M sales / $35.38-36.21 GAAP EPS range

A new DoD Inspector General report or a congressional/DoD enforcement action (refund demand, mandatory cost-data-disclosure order) is issued against TransDigm specifically (vs. the historical 2019-2022 pattern with no new action found as of this dossier)
key_adverse_facts: FQ1 FY2026 GAAP net income fell 9.7% YoY (to $445M) despite operating income rising ~7% YoY; the company's own release states this 'primarily reflects higher interest expense as a result of the increase in TransDigm's year-over-year debt'

Consolidated net debt ~$30.7bn vs TTM EBITDA As Defined ~$5.2-5.3bn = ~5.5-5.9x leverage, and rising: $1.5bn of incremental debt (incl. 6.125% senior subordinated notes) was raised 2026-04-17 to help fund acquisitions
Reported 22-23% headline revenue growth is materially M&A-driven: organic growth was only 13 percentage points of the 23% total in the most recent quarter
TD Group consolidated stockholders' deficit is -$9.8bn (negative book equity), a long-standing feature of the leveraged capital structure

Recurring DoD Inspector General/congressional scrutiny of TransDigm's aftermarket-parts pricing practices (2019-2022 findings; no new enforcement action found in 2025-2026 filings, but unresolved as a reputational/political tail risk)
data_conflicts: d4 vendor TTM free-cash-flow figure for TDG ($1.457bn) is below this dossier's own SEC-filing-derived TTM FCF ($1.927bn, from OCF minus capex per XBRL YTD tags); direction of the conflict would make TDG look even more expensive on FCF yield if the vendor figure were used
TDG.confidence_in_thesis: medium: the debt-service drag on net income and the organic-vs-M&A growth split are both directly evidenced in the company's own filings; the exact leverage multiple and forward FCF run-rate carry genuine estimation uncertainty given TDG's fiscal-quarter reporting and redeemable-NCI EPS mechanics

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for TDG (outside the original 69-name V1 universe). Own reverse DCF (equity-value basis, given negative book equity): implied 10-yr FCF-to-equity growth 12.5-14.75% across cost-of-equity 9.5-10.5% (equity value $62.4bn, TTM FCF-to-equity $1.927bn, terminal growth 3%) vs. an independent base-case estimate of ~9-12%/yr (blending guided EBITDA growth with the demonstrated debt-service drag) - implied_vs_base = above, and likely understated given the TTM FCF base predates a full year of the April-2026 debt raise.

TDG.scenario_basis: Starting TTM GAAP diluted EPS $32.96 (FQ4'25-FQ3'26); base: adjusted EPS/FCF-equivalent growth ~11%/yr (EBITDA growth mid-teens moderated by rising interest expense and integration costs), NTM P/E compresses 23.1x->21x as leverage risk gets re-priced (no dividend); bear: DoD/political scrutiny escalates or an acquisition disappoints and deleveraging stalls, EPS growth ~2%/yr, multiple compresses to 16x; bull: successful integration of JPE/VSA/Prince&Izant and intact aftermarket pricing power, EPS growth ~18%/yr, multiple holds ~25x.

TT.thesis_one_line: Top-tier commercial HVAC and data-centre-cooling franchise with record backlog and low debt, but on the programme discount rate the price implies more free-cash-flow growth than the base case, so it is a watch, not an include.
kill_criteria: Organic bookings growth turns negative YoY for two consecutive quarters (vs. +24%/+37% in Q1/Q2 2026 - a sharp, measurable reversal of the current trend)
Book-to-bill ratio falls below 100% for two consecutive quarters (vs. 123% in Q2 2026)
FY2026 guidance (currently adjusted EPS $15.20-15.30) is cut vs. the immediately preceding range at either of the next two quarterly releases
Adjusted operating margin contracts more than 150bp YoY for two consecutive quarters (vs. -20bp/-60bp in Q1/Q2 2026)
key_adverse_facts: GAAP operating margin contracted YoY in both Q1 2026 (-190bp) and Q2 2026 (-100bp), though adjusted margin was roughly flat (-20bp/-60bp) - the gap is non-GAAP acquisition/restructuring items, not an unexplained deterioration

TTM free cash flow (~$3.54bn, differenced from XBRL YTD tags) is likely inflated by a working-capital tailwind from record bookings/customer advances that may not repeat; this dossier used the more conservative NI-conversion-based FCF (~$2.95bn) for its base-case reverse DCF
Record bookings growth is concentrated in Americas Commercial HVAC/data-centre cooling - a real but narrower demand driver than 'HVAC broadly'
26.8x NTM P/E leaves the reverse DCF with essentially no valuation cushion
TT.confidence_in_thesis: medium: the bookings/backlog acceleration and guidance track record (two raises) are filing-sourced; the valuation call (implied 11.8-14.4% vs base 9-10% on Ke 9.86%, equity basis, SBC deducted) was restated in verification DV40

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for TT. Verification DV40 (programme basis: Ke 9.86% = 5.17% + Blume 1.132 x 4.14%, equity basis $99.99bn, SBC deducted) implies 11.8% (FCF $3.45bn) to 14.4% (FCF $2.86bn) 10-year FCF growth vs a 9-10% base: implied_vs_base = above, verdict INCLUDE-SMALL -> WATCH. Earlier build (WACC 8.0%, EV, no SBC) gave 7.4-9.7% = in_line.

TT.scenario_basis: Starting FY2026 guided adjusted continuing EPS midpoint $15.25; base: adjusted EPS growth ~9%/yr (matches guided algorithm), NTM P/E holds ~27x, plus ~0.9% dividend yield; bear: data-centre/commercial HVAC capex pauses and bookings roll over, EPS growth slows to ~2%/yr, multiple compresses to 20x, plus dividend; bull: electrification and data-centre cooling tailwind sustains, EPS growth ~14%/yr, multiple holds ~28x, plus dividend.

TXN.thesis_one_line: Best-in-class analog chipmaker in a genuine capex-down, cash-flow-up recovery, but on the programme discount rate the price implies more cash-flow growth than the base case, and an unresolved Chinese anti-dumping case adds risk, so it is a watch.
kill_criteria: TI's own reported TTM free-cash-flow margin (FCF/revenue) falls back below 20% for two consecutive quarterly releases
China's MOFCOM anti-dumping investigation concludes with duties or measures materially affecting TI's China unit economics (any published preliminary or final determination naming TI)
The next-quarter revenue guidance given at a release is cut (not raised or maintained) versus the immediately preceding quarter's guided range, at either of the next two earnings releases
Operating margin contracts more than 300bp YoY for two consecutive quarters (ex. any disclosed one-off item)
key_adverse_facts: China's Ministry of Commerce opened a formal anti-dumping investigation (announced Sept/Oct 2025) into US analog interface and gate-driver chips naming Texas Instruments and Analog Devices specifically; statutory conclusion date ~2026-09-13 (extendable 6 months) - unresolved as of this dossier's 2026-09-25 cutoff, against ~20% of TI revenue from China-headquartered customers and ~50% of revenue on products shipped into China
TTM buybacks fell 61% YoY (to $707M from $1.81bn) as TI prioritizes capex and the dividend over buybacks during the recovery

The reverse-DCF implied growth range (9.6-13.4%) is highly sensitive to which trailing-vs-run-rate FCF figure is used as the starting base, given TI is mid-cyclical-inflection; no normalization choice showed a comfortable margin of safety
d4 vendor TTM free-cash-flow figure ($3.545bn) materially understates the company's own reported TTM FCF ($6.534bn, 2026-07-22 release)
data_conflicts: d4 vendor 'freeCashflow' field for TXN ($3.545bn TTM) is well below TI's own reported TTM free cash flow ($6.534bn, per the 2026-07-22 earnings release); the vendor figure appears stale or computed on a different trailing window and should not be used for TXN valuation work
TXN.confidence_in_thesis: medium: revenue/margin reacceleration and guidance beats are filing-sourced; the valuation call was restated in verification DV40 (implied 12.6-20% vs base 9-10% on Ke 10.18%, CHIPS proceeds excluded, SBC deducted); China outcome unresolved

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for TXN. Verification DV40 (programme basis: Ke 10.18% = 5.17% + Blume 1.210 x 4.14%, equity basis $253.9bn, CHIPS Act proceeds excluded, SBC deducted) implies 12.6-13.2% (Q2-annualised peak FCF) to 19.6-20.3% (TTM ex-CHIPS) 10-year FCF growth vs a 9-10% base: implied_vs_base = above, verdict INCLUDE-SMALL -> WATCH. Earlier build (WACC 9.0%, terminal 3.5%, EV, TTM FCF incl. CHIPS) gave 9.6-13.4% = in_line.

TXN.scenario_basis: Starting TTM GAAP diluted EPS $6.51 (Q3'25-Q2'26); base: EPS/FCF growth ~9%/yr as the capex-down cycle continues to normalize, NTM P/E compresses 28.7x->26x, plus ~2.1% dividend yield; bear: China MOFCOM duties hit plus a cyclical semis downturn resumes, EPS roughly flat, multiple compresses to 20x, plus dividend; bull: AI-adjacent industrial/auto content sustains high growth, EPS growth ~16%/yr, multiple holds ~30x, plus dividend.
